title: Michigan Army National Guard soldiers return home from year-long deployment - NewsBreak
text:
By Mina Fuqua ,
5 hours ago
GRAND LEDGE, Mich. (WLNS) — After nearly a year overseas, dozens of Michigan Army National Guard soldiers are finally back home.
Families and loved ones gathered Wednesday at the Grand Ledge Armory to welcome home nearly 70 soldiers assigned to the Michigan Army National Guard’s 3rd Battalion, 126th Infantry Regiment.
For many families, the redeployment ceremony marked the end of months apart and the beginning of long-awaited reunions.
“The wait is hard,” said Corinne Vandermolen, whose son serves in the National Guard. “At the beginning of the deployment you think that is just unfathomable. I think not knowing what’s going on the whole time is the hardest.”
Vandermolen says her son is the first in their immediate family to join the military.
“He’s the first in our immediate family to join the military, the first of our children,” she said. “Giving us gray hair, but I’m very proud.”
Military leaders say the battalion, based out of Detroit and Wyoming, Michigan, was originally expected to return home about two months earlier.
Gen. Ravindra Wagh says the soldiers handled the extended deployment with professionalism.
“11 months and some change,” Wagh said. “The standard mobilization for our guardsmen is typically nine months in theater. They did get extended, and they handled it very well.”
According to military leaders, the soldiers were deployed in support of U.S. Central Command, also known as CENTCOM, which oversees operations in parts of the Middle East and southern Asia.
“They’ve been doing various security missions in the CENTCOM region,” Wagh said. “They did very well, and this is the first of units bringing back home to Michigan.”
Military leaders also recognized the sacrifices made by soldiers’ families throughout the deployment.
“The chain of command, we communicated with families as quickly and as often and transparently as we could,” Wagh said. “All the soldiers and families handled it exceptionally well. Professional is the word that keeps coming to mind.”
Military leaders say they are grateful to welcome the soldiers home safely after months away serving overseas.
